records.literal_gloss: Then the Jesus spoke to the crowds and to the disciples of him, \v 2 saying, On the of Moses seat sat down the scribes and the Pharisees.

en.L: Then Jesus spoke to the crowds and to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, \v 2 saying, "On the seat of Moses the scribes and the Pharisees have sat down.
en.B: Then Jesus said to the crowds and to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, \v 2 "The scribes and the Pharisees have taken Moses' seat.
en.R: Then Jesus spoke to the crowds and to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers. \v 2 He said, "The teachers of the law and the Pharisees sit in Moses' seat. This means that they have the task of teaching the law God gave through Moses.

es.L: Entonces Jesús habló a las multitudes y a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos, \v 2 diciendo: «Sobre el asiento de Moisés se han sentado los escribas y los fariseos.
es.B: Entonces Jesús dijo a las multitudes y a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos: \v 2 «Los escribas y los fariseos han ocupado el asiento de Moisés.
es.R: Entonces Jesús habló a la gente y a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} seguidores. \v 2 Les dijo: «Los maestros de la ley y los fariseos ocupan el asiento de Moisés. Esto quiere decir que tienen la tarea de enseñar la ley que Dios dio por medio de Moisés.

fr.L: Alors Jésus parla aux foules et à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples, \v 2 disant : « Sur le siège de Moïse se sont assis les scribes et les Pharisiens.
fr.B: Alors Jésus dit aux foules et à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples : \v 2 « Les scribes et les Pharisiens ont pris place sur le siège de Moïse.
fr.R: Ensuite, Jésus a parlé aux foules et à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples. \v 2 Il a dit : « Les spécialistes de la Loi et les Pharisiens sont assis sur le siège de Moïse. Cela veut dire qu’ils ont la tâche d’enseigner la Loi que Dieu a donnée par Moïse.

sw.L: Kisha Yesu alisema na makundi ya watu na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, \v 2 akisema, "Juu ya kiti cha Musa wameketi waandishi na Mafarisayo.
sw.B: Kisha Yesu aliyaambia makundi ya watu na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, \v 2 "Waandishi na Mafarisayo wamekalia kiti cha Musa.
sw.R: Kisha Yesu alizungumza na makundi ya watu na wafuasi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. \v 2 Akasema, "Walimu wa sheria na Mafarisayo wanakaa kwenye kiti cha Musa. Maana yake ni kwamba wao wana kazi ya kufundisha sheria ambayo Mungu aliitoa kupitia Musa.

vi.L: Bấy giờ Đức Giê-xu nói với đoàn dân và các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \v 2 rằng: "Các thầy thông giáo và những người Pha-ri-si đã ngồi trên ghế của Môi-se.
vi.B: Bấy giờ Đức Giê-xu nói với đoàn dân và các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: \v 2 "Các thầy thông giáo và những người Pha-ri-si đã ngồi vào ghế của Môi-se.
vi.R: Rồi Đức Giê-xu nói với đoàn dân và các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. \v 2 Ngài nói: "Các thầy dạy luật và những người Pha-ri-si ngồi trên ghế của Môi-se. Điều đó có nghĩa là họ có nhiệm vụ dạy luật pháp mà Đức Chúa Trời đã ban qua Môi-se.

ko.L: 그때에 예수께서 무리와 자기 제자들에게 말씀하셨다. \v 2 "모세의 자리에 율법학자들과 바리새파 사람들이 앉았다.
ko.B: 그때에 예수께서 무리와 제자들에게 말씀하셨다. \v 2 "율법학자들과 바리새파 사람들이 모세의 자리를 차지하고 앉아 있다.
ko.R: 그때 예수께서 무리와 제자들에게 말씀하셨다. \v 2 "율법 선생들과 바리새파 사람들은 모세의 자리에 앉아 있다. 하나님께서 모세를 통해 주신 율법을 가르치는 일을 맡고 있다는 뜻이다.

pt.L: Então Jesus falou às multidões e aos {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} discípulos, \v 2 dizendo: "Na cadeira de Moisés se sentaram os escribas e os fariseus.
pt.B: Então Jesus disse às multidões e aos {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} discípulos: \v 2 "Os escribas e os fariseus ocuparam a cadeira de Moisés.
pt.R: Então Jesus falou às multidões e aos {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} seguidores. \v 2 Ele disse: "Os mestres da Lei e os fariseus se sentam na cadeira de Moisés. Isso quer dizer que eles têm a tarefa de ensinar a Lei que Deus deu por meio de Moisés.

am.L: በዚያን ጊዜ ኢየሱስ ለሕዝቡና ለደቀ መዛሙርቱ ተናገረ፤ \v 2 እንዲህ እያለ፦ «በሙሴ ወንበር ጸሐፍትና ፈሪሳውያን ተቀምጠዋል።
am.B: በዚያን ጊዜ ኢየሱስ ለሕዝቡና ለደቀ መዛሙርቱ እንዲህ አለ፦ \v 2 «የሕግ መምህራንና ፈሪሳውያን በሙሴ ወንበር ተቀምጠዋል።
am.R: ከዚያም ኢየሱስ ለሕዝቡና ለደቀ መዛሙርቱ ተናገረ። \v 2 እንዲህ አለ፦ «የሕግ መምህራንና ፈሪሳውያን በሙሴ ወንበር ተቀምጠዋል። ይህም እግዚአብሔር በሙሴ በኩል የሰጠውን ሕግ የማስተማር ኃላፊነት አለባቸው ማለት ነው።

decisions.choice: the seat of Moses: the place of authority to teach the law of Moses
alternatives: only a stone chair of honor in the synagogue
decisions.reason: To sit in someone's seat is to hold their office. Some ancient synagogues had a stone seat of honor, and the phrase may also point to such a seat, but either way it speaks of the right to teach the law.

decisions.choice: have sat down: they have taken the seat and now hold it
alternatives: they seized the seat without any right to it
decisions.reason: The verb may hint that they took the seat on themselves. But a teacher sat to teach (5:1), and Jesus does not deny their authority in 23:3.

decisions.choice: scribes and Pharisees: the experts in the law and the party devoted to keeping it strictly
decisions.reason: Scribes were trained teachers of the law of Moses; many of them were Pharisees. The Pharisees were a movement devoted to keeping the law in detail (see 3:7).

decisions.choice: have taken Moses' seat
alternatives: sit on the seat of Moses
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of the seat and the sense of the verb, that they have taken it and now hold it.

decisions.choice: This means that they have the task of teaching the law God gave through Moses
decisions.reason: Readable says what the seat stands for, from the first meaning decision.

decisions.choice: the teachers of the law
decisions.reason: As in 2:4, Readable says what the scribes were.

decisions.choice: los escribas (L, B); los maestros de la ley (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide rendering: "escribas" is the established Spanish word for these experts in the law (meaning decision m3); Readable says what they did, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on separate pronouns and possessives (sus, él)
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Spanish usually leaves the subject pronoun out, so the setting covers fewer words than in English. This holds for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); speech keeps its own tenses at every level
decisions.reason: As in John, Mark and Luke, and in Matthew 11. The rest of the chapter is Jesus's speech.

decisions.choice: le siège de Moïse; les scribes (L, B), les spécialistes de la Loi (R); disciples at every level
decisions.reason: "Chaire" today suggests a pulpit or a university chair; "siège" keeps the plain picture of a seat of authority (m1). The scribes take the term sheet's forms, Readable following the English "teachers of the law", as in Luke 11:53. French keeps "disciples" at Readable, as Mark's French does, where English says "followers".

decisions.choice: waandishi (L, B); walimu wa sheria (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide rendering: "waandishi" is the established Swahili word for these experts in the law (meaning decision m3); Readable says what they did, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on free pronouns and possessives (wake, naye)
decisions.reason: Swahili marks most pronouns inside the verb, and a prefix cannot take a capital, so the setting covers fewer words than in English. This applies to the whole passage.

decisions.choice: "các con" for the crowds and disciples Jesus teaches (23:1-12); "nói" for his speaking
decisions.reason: As settled for Matthew: Jesus addresses disciples and the crowd he is teaching as "các con"; "các người" is kept for the scribes and Pharisees whom he addresses from 23:13.

decisions.choice: "các thầy thông giáo" (L, B); "các thầy dạy luật" (R); "những người Pha-ri-si"
decisions.reason: The settled Gospel terms, as in Mark 12:38 and Matthew 15:1. "Ghế của Môi-se" keeps the picture at every level; Readable says what it meant, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean, through Matthew 23:1-12; Jesus speaks to the crowds and the disciples in 해라체
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters; respect for Jesus is carried by -시- and 께서 (style guide, sections 4 and 7).

decisions.choice: "모세의 자리" at every level, explained at Readable; "율법학자들" (L, B), "율법 선생들" (R)
decisions.reason: The seat is the place of authority to teach the law (meaning decision); the scribes as in the Korean Matthew 7:29 and 17:10.

decisions.choice: a cadeira de Moisés
decisions.reason: "Cátedra" is the learned word for a teacher's chair and keeps the sense of office, but few readers know it. "Cadeira" is plain, and Brazilians still speak of a professor's "cadeira" for a teaching post, so the picture carries the same sense; the meaning note explains it.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans: the possessive suffix ("ደቀ መዛሙርቱ", his disciples) and "እርሱ" stay as they are
alternatives: a capitalised pronoun, as the English alternative
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the reader setting that capitalises pronouns for God and Christ has nothing to change in Amharic. The English spans in this passage have no Amharic counterpart.

decisions.choice: "ጸሐፍት" (L); "የሕግ መምህራን" (teachers of the law, B, R)
decisions.reason: The scribes were the teachers and interpreters of the law of Moses, not copyists. Literal keeps the traditional word "ጸሐፍት" (writers); Balanced and Readable say what they did, so a reader does not take them for clerks. "ደቀ መዛሙርት" stays at every level, though the English Readable says "followers".

source.text: πάντα οὖν ὅσα ἐὰν εἴπωσιν ὑμῖν ποιήσατε καὶ τηρεῖτε, κατὰ δὲ τὰ ἔργα αὐτῶν μὴ ποιεῖτε, λέγουσιν γὰρ καὶ οὐ ποιοῦσιν.

records.literal_gloss: All things therefore as many as they may tell you do and keep, according to but the works of them not do; they say for and not do.

en.L: So whatever they tell you, do and keep all of it; but do not do according to their works, for they say [things] and do not do [them].
en.B: So practice and keep whatever they tell you. But do not follow their example, because they do not live by what they teach.
en.R: So obey them and do everything they tell you. But do not do the things they do. They tell people what to do, but they do not do it themselves.

es.L: Así que todo cuanto {{plural_you:les|os}} digan, {{plural_you:háganlo|hacedlo}} y {{plural_you:guárdenlo|guardadlo}}; pero no {{plural_you:actúen|actuéis}} según sus obras, porque dicen [cosas] y no [las] hacen.
es.B: Por eso, {{plural_you:pongan|poned}} en práctica y {{plural_you:guarden|guardad}} todo lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} digan. Pero no {{plural_you:sigan|sigáis}} su ejemplo, porque no viven conforme a lo que enseñan.
es.R: Así que {{plural_you:obedézcanlos|obedecedlos}} y {{plural_you:hagan|haced}} todo lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} digan. Pero no {{plural_you:hagan|hagáis}} lo que ellos hacen. Les dicen a los demás lo que tienen que hacer, pero ellos mismos no lo hacen.

fr.L: Donc tout ce qu’ils vous diront, faites-le et gardez-le ; mais ne faites pas selon leurs œuvres, car ils disent et ne font pas.
fr.B: Mettez donc en pratique et gardez tout ce qu’ils vous disent. Mais ne suivez pas leur exemple, car ils ne vivent pas selon ce qu’ils enseignent.
fr.R: Alors obéissez-leur et faites tout ce qu’ils vous disent. Mais ne faites pas ce qu’ils font. Ils disent aux gens ce qu’il faut faire, mais eux-mêmes ne le font pas.

sw.L: Basi yote watakayowaambia, yafanyeni na kuyashika; lakini msifanye kulingana na matendo yao, kwa sababu wanasema [mambo] na hawayafanyi.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo, fanyeni na kushika kila wanachowaambia. Lakini msifuate mfano wao, kwa sababu hawaishi kwa yale wanayofundisha.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo watiini, na mfanye kila kitu wanachowaambia. Lakini msifanye yale wanayoyafanya wao. Wanawaambia watu wengine la kufanya, lakini wao wenyewe hawalifanyi.

vi.L: Vậy mọi điều gì họ bảo các con, hãy làm và giữ lấy; nhưng đừng làm theo việc làm của họ, vì họ nói mà không làm.
vi.B: Vậy, những gì họ dạy các con, hãy làm và tuân giữ; nhưng đừng bắt chước việc họ làm, vì họ nói mà không làm.
vi.R: Vậy các con hãy vâng theo và làm mọi điều họ dạy. Nhưng đừng làm theo những việc họ làm. Họ bảo người khác phải làm điều này điều kia, nhưng chính họ lại không làm.

ko.L: 그러므로 그들이 너희에게 말하는 것은 무엇이든지 다 행하고 지켜라. 그러나 그들의 행위를 따라 행하지는 마라. 그들은 말만 하고 행하지 않기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그러므로 그들이 너희에게 가르치는 것은 무엇이든지 지키고 행하여라. 그러나 그들이 하는 행동은 본받지 마라. 그들은 말만 하고 그대로 살지 않는다.
ko.R: 그러니 그들이 가르치는 것은 모두 그대로 지켜라. 그러나 그들이 하는 대로 따라 하지는 마라. 그들은 남에게 하라고 말만 하고 자기들은 하지 않는다.

pt.L: Portanto, tudo o que eles lhes disserem, façam e guardem; mas não façam conforme as obras deles, pois dizem [as coisas] e não [as] fazem.
pt.B: Portanto, pratiquem e guardem tudo o que eles lhes disserem. Mas não sigam o exemplo deles, porque eles não vivem o que ensinam.
pt.R: Por isso, obedeçam a eles e façam tudo o que eles mandarem. Mas não façam o que eles fazem. Eles dizem às pessoas o que fazer, mas eles mesmos não fazem.

am.L: እንግዲህ የሚነግሯችሁን ሁሉ አድርጉ፤ ጠብቁም፤ እንደ ሥራቸው ግን አታድርጉ፤ ይናገራሉና፣ አያደርጉምም።
am.B: ስለዚህ የሚነግሯችሁን ሁሉ በተግባር ፈጽሙ፤ ጠብቁትም። ነገር ግን እነርሱ የሚያደርጉትን አትከተሉ፤ የሚያስተምሩትን ራሳቸው አይኖሩበትምና።
am.R: ስለዚህ ታዘዟቸው፤ የሚነግሯችሁንም ሁሉ አድርጉ። ነገር ግን እነርሱ የሚያደርጉትን አታድርጉ። ሰዎች ምን ማድረግ እንዳለባቸው ይነግራሉ፤ እነርሱ ግን ራሳቸው አያደርጉትም።

decisions.choice: whatever they tell you: what they teach from Moses' seat, the law of Moses itself
alternatives: every ruling they make, without exception
an ironic command not meant seriously
decisions.reason: Jesus goes on to reject some of their rulings (23:16-22) and has already warned against their teaching (15:3-9; 16:6, 12). The command most likely covers what they pass on from the law. How far it reaches is not stated, and some read it as irony.

decisions.choice: they say and do not do: they teach but do not live by their teaching
alternatives: they make promises they do not keep
decisions.reason: The contrast is between their words as teachers and their works, which 23:4-7 go on to describe.

decisions.choice: do not follow their example (B); do not do the things they do (R)
alternatives: do not do according to their works
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly what it means to act according to their works.

decisions.choice: plural_you spans on every plural "you" (les|os, háganlo|hacedlo)
decisions.reason: Spanish has two plural forms of "you", Latin American "ustedes" and Peninsular "vosotros"; the setting chooses between them. English has no such choice, so these spans have no English counterpart. The same throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: "말하는 것" (L); "가르치는 것" (B, R)
decisions.reason: What they say from Moses' seat is their teaching of the law (meaning decision).

source.text: δεσμεύουσιν δὲ φορτία βαρέα καὶ ἐπιτιθέασιν ἐπὶ τοὺς ὤμους τῶν ἀνθρώπων, αὐτοὶ δὲ τῷ δακτύλῳ αὐτῶν οὐ θέλουσιν κινῆσαι αὐτά.

records.literal_gloss: They tie up and burdens heavy and lay on the shoulders of the men, they themselves but with the finger of them not are willing to move them.

en.L: And they tie up heavy burdens and lay [them] on the shoulders of {{gender:people|men}}, but they themselves are not willing to move them with their finger.
en.B: They bundle up heavy loads and pile them on the shoulders of others, but they refuse to move those loads even with a finger.
en.R: They make rules that are like heavy loads, and they put them on people's shoulders. But they will not do even the smallest thing to help people carry them.

es.L: Y atan cargas pesadas y [las] ponen sobre los hombros de {{gender:la gente|los hombres}}, pero ellos mismos no quieren moverlas con su dedo.
es.B: Atan fardos pesados y los cargan sobre los hombros de los demás, pero ellos se niegan a moverlos siquiera con un dedo.
es.R: Hacen reglas que son como cargas pesadas, y se las ponen a la gente sobre los hombros. Pero no hacen ni lo más mínimo para ayudarlos a llevarlas.

fr.L: Ils lient des fardeaux pesants et [les] mettent sur les épaules des {{gender:gens|hommes}}, mais eux-mêmes ne veulent pas les remuer de leur doigt.
fr.B: Ils attachent de lourdes charges et les entassent sur les épaules des autres, mais eux refusent de les déplacer, ne serait-ce que du doigt.
fr.R: Ils font des règles qui sont comme de lourdes charges, et ils les mettent sur les épaules des gens. Mais eux-mêmes ne veulent rien faire, même pas la plus petite chose, pour aider les gens à les porter.

sw.L: Na wanafunga mizigo mizito na kuiweka juu ya mabega ya watu, lakini wao wenyewe hawataki kuisogeza kwa kidole chao.
sw.B: Wanafunga mizigo mizito na kuirundika juu ya mabega ya wengine, lakini wao wenyewe wanakataa hata kuisogeza kwa kidole.
sw.R: Wanaweka sheria ambazo ni kama mizigo mizito, nao wanaziweka juu ya mabega ya watu. Lakini hawafanyi hata jambo dogo kabisa kuwasaidia watu kuzibeba.

vi.L: Họ buộc những gánh nặng rồi đặt lên vai người ta, còn chính họ thì không muốn động ngón tay mình vào.
vi.B: Họ bó những gánh nặng nề rồi chất lên vai người khác, còn chính họ thì một ngón tay cũng không chịu động đến.
vi.R: Họ đặt ra những luật lệ nặng nề như những gánh nặng, rồi chất lên vai người ta. Nhưng chính họ lại không chịu làm một chút gì để giúp người ta mang những gánh ấy.

ko.L: 그들은 무거운 짐들을 묶어서 사람들의 어깨에 지우지만, 자기들은 그것들을 손가락으로 움직이려고도 하지 않는다.
ko.B: 그들은 무거운 짐을 묶어서 남의 어깨에 지우면서, 자기들은 그 짐을 손가락 하나 까딱하여 옮기려고도 하지 않는다.
ko.R: 그들은 지키기 어려운 규칙들을 무거운 짐처럼 만들어서 사람들의 어깨에 지운다. 그러나 사람들이 그 짐을 지도록 도와주는 일은 조금도 하지 않는다.

pt.L: E amarram fardos pesados e [os] põem sobre os ombros {{gender:das pessoas|dos homens}}, mas eles mesmos não querem movê-los com o dedo deles.
pt.B: Eles amarram cargas pesadas e as colocam sobre os ombros dos outros, mas não estão dispostos a movê-las nem com um dedo.
pt.R: Eles fazem regras que são como cargas pesadas e as colocam nos ombros das pessoas. Mas não fazem nem a menor coisa para ajudar as pessoas a carregá-las.

am.L: ከባድ ሸክሞችንም ያስራሉ፤ በሰዎችም ትከሻ ላይ ይጭኗቸዋል፤ እነርሱ ራሳቸው ግን በጣታቸው ሊያንቀሳቅሷቸው ፈቃደኞች አይደሉም።
am.B: ከባድ ሸክሞችን አስረው በሌሎች ሰዎች ትከሻ ላይ ይከምራሉ፤ ራሳቸው ግን እነዚያን ሸክሞች በአንድ ጣት እንኳ ለማንቀሳቀስ እምቢ ይላሉ።
am.R: እንደ ከባድ ሸክም የሆኑ ሕጎችን ያወጣሉ፤ በሰዎችም ትከሻ ላይ ይጭኗቸዋል። ነገር ግን ሰዎች እንዲሸከሟቸው ለመርዳት ትንሽ ነገር እንኳ አያደርጉም።

decisions.choice: heavy burdens: demanding rules for keeping the law
decisions.reason: The loads are the many detailed rules the teachers lay on people. Jesus offers a light burden instead (11:28-30).

decisions.choice: not willing to move them with a finger: they make no effort at all to help
alternatives: they will not keep the rules themselves
they will not ease the rules
decisions.reason: The picture is of refusing even the smallest effort. It may mean that they give no help to those who carry the rules, or that they will not lighten them; the first fits the picture best.

decisions.choice: {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: The word means people in general, so the inclusive form is the default.

decisions.choice: rules that are like heavy loads
decisions.reason: Readable says what the loads stand for, from the first meaning decision.

decisions.choice: {{gender:gens|hommes}} (L), here and in 23:5, 23:13 and 23:28
decisions.reason: As in Luke 11:46: the word means people in general, and after "les épaules des" or "vus des" French says "gens"; "hommes" stays as the traditional alternative.

decisions.choice: "người ta" (L, R), "người khác" (B), with no gender span (also 23:5)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese words for people are already inclusive (style guide section 7), so the English people/men setting has nothing to choose between.

decisions.choice: "không muốn động ngón tay" (L, B); "không chịu làm một chút gì để giúp" (R)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese uses the same picture of not lifting a finger for making no effort at all (meaning decision); Readable says it plainly.

decisions.choice: No gender span: "사람들", "남"
alternatives: a span as in the English Literal
decisions.reason: Korean "사람" is already inclusive.

decisions.choice: "손가락 하나 까딱하다" (B)
decisions.reason: The Korean idiom says the same as the Greek picture: no effort at all (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "ሰዎች" (people) with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span like the English {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: The Amharic word "ሰዎች" already means people, women and men, so there is no second wording for the gender setting to offer. The same holds for "ሰዎች" in 23:5-7.

source.text: πάντα δὲ τὰ ἔργα αὐτῶν ποιοῦσιν πρὸς τὸ θεαθῆναι τοῖς ἀνθρώποις· πλατύνουσι γὰρ τὰ φυλακτήρια αὐτῶν καὶ μεγαλύνουσι τὰ κράσπεδα, φιλοῦσι δὲ τὴν πρωτοκλισίαν ἐν τοῖς δείπνοις καὶ τὰς πρωτοκαθεδρίας ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καὶ τοὺς ἀσπασμοὺς ἐν ταῖς ἀγοραῖς καὶ καλεῖσθαι ὑπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων· Ῥαββί.

records.literal_gloss: All but the works of them they do in order to be seen by the men; they broaden for the phylacteries of them and enlarge the tassels, \v 6 they love and the chief place at the dinners and the first seats in the synagogues \v 7 and the greetings in the marketplaces and to be called by the men, Rabbi.

en.L: And they do all their works to be seen by {{gender:people|men}}; for they broaden their phylacteries and enlarge the tassels, \v 6 and they love the chief place at the dinners and the first seats in the synagogues \v 7 and the greetings in the marketplaces, and to be called 'Rabbi' by {{gender:people|men}}.
en.B: All their deeds are done for others to watch. They widen their phylacteries and lengthen their tassels. \v 6 They are fond of the seat of honor at banquets and the front seats in the synagogues, \v 7 of respectful greetings in the marketplaces, and of hearing people address them as 'Rabbi.'
en.R: Everything they do, they do so that people will see them. They wear small boxes with words of Scripture in them, and they make these boxes extra wide. They make the tassels on the corners of their clothes extra long. \v 6 At big dinners they love to sit in the most important places. In the synagogues they love the best seats. \v 7 They love it when people greet them with respect in the marketplaces and call them 'Rabbi,' which means 'Teacher.'

es.L: Y hacen todas sus obras para ser vistos por {{gender:la gente|los hombres}}; pues hacen anchas sus filacterias y agrandan los flecos, \v 6 y aman el puesto principal en las cenas y los primeros asientos en las sinagogas, \v 7 y los saludos en los mercados, y ser llamados “Rabí” por {{gender:la gente|los hombres}}.
es.B: Todo lo que hacen lo hacen para que los demás los vean. Llevan filacterias más anchas y flecos más largos. \v 6 Les gusta el lugar de honor en los banquetes y los asientos delanteros en las sinagogas, \v 7 los saludos respetuosos en los mercados y que la gente los llame “Rabí”.
es.R: Todo lo que hacen, lo hacen para que la gente los vea. Llevan unas cajitas con palabras de las Escrituras, y las hacen muy anchas. Les ponen flecos muy largos a las esquinas de su ropa. \v 6 En las grandes cenas les encanta sentarse en los lugares más importantes. En las sinagogas les encantan los mejores asientos. \v 7 Les encanta que la gente los salude con respeto en los mercados y que los llame “Rabí”, que quiere decir “Maestro”.

fr.L: Et toutes leurs œuvres, ils les font pour être vus des {{gender:gens|hommes}} ; car ils élargissent leurs phylactères et allongent les houppes, \v 6 et ils aiment la première place dans les dîners et les premiers sièges dans les synagogues \v 7 et les salutations sur les places publiques, et être appelés “Rabbi” par les {{gender:gens|hommes}}.
fr.B: Toutes leurs actions, ils les font pour que les autres les regardent. Ils élargissent leurs phylactères et allongent leurs houppes. \v 6 Ils aiment la place d’honneur dans les banquets et les premiers sièges dans les synagogues, \v 7 les salutations respectueuses sur les places du marché, et ils aiment entendre les gens les appeler “Rabbi”.
fr.R: Tout ce qu’ils font, ils le font pour que les gens les voient. Ils portent de petites boîtes avec des paroles de l’Écriture à l’intérieur, et ils les font très larges. Ils font aussi très longues les franges aux coins de leurs vêtements. \v 6 Dans les grands repas, ils aiment s’asseoir aux places les plus importantes. Dans les synagogues, ils aiment les meilleures places. \v 7 Ils aiment que les gens les saluent avec respect sur les places du marché et les appellent “Rabbi”, ce qui veut dire “Maître”.

sw.L: Na matendo yao yote wanayafanya ili waonekane na watu; kwa maana wanapanua visanduku vyao vya maandiko na kurefusha vishada, \v 6 tena wanapenda nafasi ya kwanza katika karamu na viti vya mbele katika masinagogi \v 7 na salamu sokoni, na kuitwa 'Rabi' na watu.
sw.B: Matendo yao yote wanayafanya ili watu wawatazame. Wanapanua visanduku vyao vya maandiko na kurefusha vishada vya mavazi yao. \v 6 Wanapenda viti vya heshima katika karamu na viti vya mbele katika masinagogi, \v 7 salamu za heshima sokoni, na kusikia watu wakiwaita 'Rabi.'
sw.R: Kila wanachofanya, wanakifanya ili watu wawaone. Wanavaa visanduku vidogo vyenye maneno ya Maandiko, na wanavifanya kuwa vipana kupita kiasi. Wanarefusha sana vishada vilivyo kwenye pembe za nguo zao. \v 6 Kwenye karamu kubwa wanapenda kukaa mahali pa watu muhimu. Katika masinagogi wanapenda viti bora. \v 7 Wanapenda watu wawasalimu kwa heshima sokoni na kuwaita 'Rabi,' maana yake 'Mwalimu.'

vi.L: Và họ làm mọi việc của mình để được người ta nhìn thấy; vì họ làm cho hộp kinh của mình rộng ra và tua áo dài ra, \v 6 và họ thích chỗ ngồi trên hết trong các bữa tiệc, những ghế đầu trong các nhà hội, \v 7 và những lời chào hỏi ở các nơi chợ, và được người ta gọi là 'Ra-bi.'
vi.B: Họ làm mọi việc chỉ để cho người ta xem. Họ đeo hộp kinh thật to và may tua áo thật dài. \v 6 Họ thích ngồi chỗ danh dự trong các bữa tiệc và hàng ghế đầu trong các nhà hội. \v 7 Họ thích được người ta chào hỏi kính cẩn nơi phố chợ, và được gọi là 'Ra-bi.'
vi.R: Mọi việc họ làm đều là để người ta nhìn thấy họ. Họ đeo những cái hộp nhỏ đựng lời Kinh Thánh trên trán và trên cánh tay, và họ làm những hộp ấy thật to. Họ làm những cái tua ở góc áo choàng thật dài. \v 6 Trong các bữa tiệc lớn, họ thích ngồi ở những chỗ quan trọng nhất. Trong các nhà hội, họ thích ngồi những ghế tốt nhất. \v 7 Họ thích được người ta chào hỏi kính trọng ngoài chợ, và gọi họ là 'Ra-bi,' nghĩa là 'Thầy.'

ko.L: 그리고 그들은 자기들의 모든 행위를 사람들에게 보이려고 한다. 그들은 자기들의 성구함을 넓게 만들고 옷술을 길게 늘인다. \v 6 그리고 잔치에서는 윗자리를, 회당에서는 높은 자리를 좋아하고, \v 7 장터에서 인사 받기와 사람들에게 '랍비'라고 불리기를 [좋아한다].
ko.B: 그들이 하는 일은 모두 사람들에게 보이려는 것이다. 그들은 성구함을 넓게 만들고 옷술을 길게 늘인다. \v 6 잔치에서는 윗자리에, 회당에서는 높은 자리에 앉기를 좋아하고, \v 7 장터에서 깍듯한 인사 받기와 사람들이 자기를 '랍비'라고 불러 주기를 좋아한다.
ko.R: 그들은 무엇이든지 사람들에게 보이려고 한다. 그들은 성경 말씀을 넣은 작은 상자를 이마와 팔에 매는데, 그 상자를 남보다 넓게 만든다. 또 겉옷 귀퉁이에 다는 술을 남보다 길게 늘인다. \v 6 큰 잔치에서는 가장 귀한 자리에 앉기를 좋아한다. 회당에서도 가장 좋은 자리에 앉기를 좋아한다. \v 7 장터에서 사람들이 자기에게 공손히 인사하는 것을 좋아한다. 또 사람들이 자기를 '랍비', 곧 '선생님'이라고 불러 주는 것을 좋아한다.

pt.L: E fazem todas as suas obras para serem vistos {{gender:pelas pessoas|pelos homens}}; pois alargam os seus filactérios e aumentam as franjas, \v 6 e amam o lugar de honra nos banquetes e as primeiras cadeiras nas sinagogas \v 7 e as saudações nas praças, e ser chamados de 'Rabi' {{gender:pelas pessoas|pelos homens}}.
pt.B: Tudo o que fazem é para os outros verem. Eles alargam os seus filactérios e alongam as franjas das suas roupas. \v 6 Gostam do lugar de honra nos banquetes e dos primeiros assentos nas sinagogas, \v 7 das saudações respeitosas nas praças e de ouvir as pessoas chamá-los de 'Rabi'.
pt.R: Tudo o que eles fazem, fazem para que as pessoas os vejam. Eles usam caixinhas com palavras das Escrituras dentro e fazem essas caixinhas bem largas. Fazem bem compridas as franjas nos cantos das suas roupas. \v 6 Nos grandes jantares, eles adoram sentar nos lugares mais importantes. Nas sinagogas, adoram os melhores assentos. \v 7 Eles adoram quando as pessoas os cumprimentam com respeito nas praças e os chamam de 'Rabi', que quer dizer 'Mestre'.

am.L: ሥራቸውንም ሁሉ በሰዎች ለመታየት ያደርጋሉ፤ ክታቦቻቸውን ያሰፋሉና፣ ዘርፎቹንም ያስረዝማሉ፤ \v 6 በግብዣዎችም የክብር ቦታን፣ በምኩራቦችም የፊት ወንበሮችን ይወዳሉ፤ \v 7 በገበያ ቦታዎችም ሰላምታን፣ በሰዎችም “ረቢ” ተብለው መጠራትን [ይወዳሉ]።
am.B: ሥራቸውን ሁሉ የሚያደርጉት ሰዎች እንዲያዩአቸው ነው። ክታቦቻቸውን ያሰፋሉ፤ የልብሳቸውንም ዘርፍ ያስረዝማሉ። \v 6 በግብዣ የክብር ቦታን፣ በምኩራቦችም የፊት ወንበሮችን ይወዳሉ፤ \v 7 በገበያ ቦታዎች የአክብሮት ሰላምታ ሲቀርብላቸውና ሰዎች “ረቢ” ብለው ሲጠሯቸውም ደስ ይላቸዋል።
am.R: የሚያደርጉትን ሁሉ የሚያደርጉት ሰዎች እንዲያዩአቸው ብለው ነው። የቅዱሳት መጻሕፍት ቃል የተጻፈባቸው ትናንሽ ሣጥኖች ያስራሉ፤ እነዚህንም ሣጥኖች በጣም ሰፋ ያደርጓቸዋል። በልብሳቸው ጫፍ ላይ ያሉትንም ዘርፎች በጣም ያስረዝማሉ። \v 6 በትልቅ ግብዣ ላይ በጣም በተከበረው ቦታ መቀመጥ ይወዳሉ። በምኩራቦችም ምርጥ የሆኑትን ወንበሮች ይወዳሉ። \v 7 በገበያ ቦታዎች ሰዎች በአክብሮት ሰላም ሲሏቸውና “ረቢ” ብለው ሲጠሯቸው ደስ ይላቸዋል። ረቢ ማለት “መምህር” ማለት ነው።

decisions.choice: phylacteries: small leather cases holding passages of the law, tied on the forehead and the arm
decisions.reason: Jews kept Deuteronomy 6:8 and 11:18 by binding small cases with passages of the law to the forehead and the arm for prayer. The word could also mean an amulet, but here it is these cases. Wide ones were easily noticed.

decisions.choice: tassels: the tassels worn at the corners of the cloak
decisions.reason: The law told Israelites to wear tassels to remind them of God's commands (Numbers 15:38-39). Jesus wore them too (9:20; 14:36); the fault is in making them long to be seen.

decisions.choice: the chief place, the first seats, the greetings: public marks of honor
decisions.reason: At a feast the places next to the host went to the most honored guests (Luke 14:7-10). In the synagogue the leading seats faced the people. In the marketplace a respected teacher was greeted first and with titles.

decisions.choice: Rabbi: a title of respect for a teacher, literally "my great one"
decisions.reason: The word is Aramaic. John 1:38 explains it as "Teacher".

decisions.choice: phylacteries
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the name of the object, which a reader can look up; the meaning decision explains it.

decisions.choice: small boxes with words of Scripture in them; which means 'Teacher'
decisions.reason: Readable says what phylacteries were and what the title means.

decisions.choice: {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: The word means people in general, so the inclusive form is the default.

decisions.choice: les houppes (L, B); les franges aux coins de leurs vêtements (R); “Rabbi”, ce qui veut dire “Maître” (R)
decisions.reason: The tassels worn at the corners of the cloak (m2) are "houppes" in French; "franges" would suggest a fringe along the whole hem, but it is the plainer word for Readable, which says where they were. Readable explains "Rabbi" with "Maître", the word used for the address "Teacher" (22:16).

decisions.choice: visanduku vya maandiko (phylacteries); vishada (tassels)
decisions.reason: The phylacteries were small cases holding passages of the law (meaning decision m1). "Hirizi" would call them charms worn for protection, which they were not; "visanduku vya maandiko" says what they were. "Vishada" are tassels (meaning decision m2); "matamvua" is a fringe.

decisions.choice: "hộp kinh" (L, B); "những cái hộp nhỏ đựng lời Kinh Thánh trên trán và trên cánh tay" (R); "tua áo"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese has no everyday word for phylacteries; "hộp kinh" says what they were, small cases holding passages of the law (meaning decision), and Readable describes them where they were worn. "Thẻ bài" (1926) now reads as a tag or badge.

decisions.choice: "Ra-bi" at every level; Readable adds "nghĩa là 'Thầy'"
decisions.reason: "Ra-bi" is the style guide's form; the title is the point of 23:7-8, so it is kept and Readable explains it, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "성구함" (L, B), described at Readable; "옷술" (L, B), "겉옷 귀퉁이에 다는 술" (R)
decisions.reason: Small leather cases holding passages of the law (meaning decision); "성구함" says what they are, where "경문" is the older church word. The tassels as in the Korean Matthew 9:20.

decisions.choice: [좋아한다] (L)
decisions.reason: Korean needs the verb again at the end of the list.

decisions.choice: as praças
decisions.reason: The marketplace was a town's open public square, where people met as well as traded. "Praça" is that place in a Brazilian town; "mercado" and "feira" suggest only buying and selling.

decisions.choice: as franjas
decisions.reason: "Franjas" is the familiar word for the fringes the law commanded (Numbers 15:38); "borlas" is exact but rare. Balanced and Readable add where they hang, on the clothes.

decisions.choice: "ክታብ" for the phylacteries; "ዘርፍ" (fringe) for the tassels
decisions.reason: A "ክታብ" is a small case or roll with written words worn on the body, which is what a phylactery was. Ethiopian readers may think of an amulet, so Readable describes the object (small boxes with words of Scripture), and a reviewer may prefer a description at Balanced too.

decisions.choice: "[ይወዳሉ]" repeated in verse 7
alternatives: moving "they love" to the end of verse 7
decisions.reason: The Greek "they love" stands at the start of verse 6 and governs the objects of verse 7. Amharic puts the verb last, so it closes verse 6, and verse 7 needs it again to keep its own content after its marker.

source.text: ὑμεῖς δὲ μὴ κληθῆτε· Ῥαββί, εἷς γάρ ἐστιν ὑμῶν ὁ διδάσκαλος, πάντες δὲ ὑμεῖς ἀδελφοί ἐστε·

records.literal_gloss: You but not be called Rabbi, one for is of you the teacher, all and you brothers are;

en.L: But you, do not be called 'Rabbi,' for one is your teacher, and you are all {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}.
en.B: But as for you, do not let anyone call you 'Rabbi.' There is one who is your teacher, and all of you are {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} together.
en.R: But do not let people call you 'Rabbi.' You have only one teacher. And you are all equal, like {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} in one family.

es.L: Pero {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, no {{plural_you:sean llamados|seáis llamados}} “Rabí”, porque uno es {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} maestro, y todos {{plural_you:ustedes son|vosotros sois}} hermanos.
es.B: Pero en cuanto a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, no {{plural_you:dejen|dejéis}} que nadie {{plural_you:los|os}} llame “Rabí”. Uno solo es {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} maestro, y todos {{plural_you:ustedes son|vosotros sois}} hermanos.
es.R: Pero no {{plural_you:dejen|dejéis}} que la gente {{plural_you:los|os}} llame “Rabí”. {{plural_you:Tienen|Tenéis}} un solo maestro. Y todos {{plural_you:son|sois}} iguales, como hermanos de una misma familia.

fr.L: Mais vous, ne vous faites pas appeler “Rabbi”, car un seul est votre maître, et vous, vous êtes tous {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}.
fr.B: Mais vous, ne laissez personne vous appeler “Rabbi”. Vous n’avez qu’un seul maître, et vous êtes tous {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}.
fr.R: Mais ne laissez pas les gens vous appeler “Rabbi”. Vous n’avez qu’un seul maître. Et vous êtes tous égaux, comme des {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} dans une même famille.

sw.L: Lakini ninyi, msiitwe 'Rabi,' kwa sababu mmoja ndiye mwalimu wenu, na ninyi nyote ni ndugu.
sw.B: Lakini ninyi, msikubali mtu yeyote awaite 'Rabi.' Yupo mmoja tu aliye mwalimu wenu, na ninyi nyote ni ndugu mlio pamoja.
sw.R: Lakini msikubali watu wawaite 'Rabi.' Mna mwalimu mmoja tu. Na nyote mko sawa, kama ndugu katika familia moja.

vi.L: Nhưng các con, đừng để người ta gọi mình là 'Ra-bi,' vì các con chỉ có một Thầy, và tất cả các con đều là {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}}.
vi.B: Còn các con, đừng để ai gọi mình là 'Ra-bi,' vì các con chỉ có một Thầy, và tất cả các con đều là {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}} với nhau.
vi.R: Nhưng các con đừng để người ta gọi mình là 'Ra-bi.' Các con chỉ có một Thầy mà thôi. Và tất cả các con đều ngang hàng nhau, như {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}} trong một gia đình.

ko.L: 그러나 너희는 '랍비'라고 불리지 마라. 너희의 선생은 한 분뿐이고, 너희는 모두 {{gender:형제자매|형제}}이다.
ko.B: 그러나 너희는 누가 너희를 '랍비'라고 부르게 하지 마라. 너희의 선생은 한 분뿐이시고, 너희는 모두 서로 {{gender:형제자매|형제}}이다.
ko.R: 그러나 너희는 사람들이 너희를 '랍비'라고 부르게 하지 마라. 너희의 선생님은 오직 한 분뿐이다. 너희는 모두 한 가족인 {{gender:형제자매|형제}}처럼 서로 같다.

pt.L: Mas vocês, não sejam chamados de 'Rabi', pois um só é o mestre de vocês, e todos vocês são {{gender:irmãos e irmãs|irmãos}}.
pt.B: Quanto a vocês, não deixem que ninguém os chame de 'Rabi'. Há um só que é o mestre de vocês, e todos vocês são {{gender:irmãos e irmãs|irmãos}} entre si.
pt.R: Mas não deixem que as pessoas chamem vocês de 'Rabi'. Vocês têm um só mestre. E vocês são todos iguais, como {{gender:irmãos e irmãs|irmãos}} numa mesma família.

am.L: እናንተ ግን “ረቢ” ተብላችሁ አትጠሩ፤ መምህራችሁ አንድ ነውና፤ እናንተም ሁላችሁ {{gender:ወንድሞችና እኅቶች|ወንድሞች}} ናችሁ።
am.B: እናንተ ግን ማንም “ረቢ” ብሎ እንዲጠራችሁ አትፍቀዱ። መምህራችሁ አንድ ብቻ ነው፤ ሁላችሁም በአንድነት {{gender:ወንድሞችና እኅቶች|ወንድሞች}} ናችሁ።
am.R: እናንተ ግን ሰዎች “ረቢ” ብለው እንዲጠሯችሁ አትፍቀዱ። ያላችሁ መምህር አንድ ብቻ ነው። ሁላችሁም በአንድ ቤተሰብ እንዳሉ {{gender:ወንድሞችና እኅቶች|ወንድሞች}} እኩሎች ናችሁ።

decisions.choice: you: emphatic, the disciples set against the scribes and Pharisees
decisions.reason: The pronoun is written out and stands first. Jesus now turns from the leaders to his own followers.

decisions.choice: the one teacher: Jesus himself
decisions.reason: 23:10 names the one instructor as the Christ, and the disciples call Jesus teacher. Some take the teacher here as God, since 23:9 speaks of the Father.

decisions.choice: brothers: fellow members of one family under God, women and men alike
decisions.reason: As in 12:49-50, those who follow Jesus are one family. None of them stands above the others.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The disciples addressed include women as well as men (12:49-50), so the inclusive form is the default.

decisions.choice: you are all equal, like ... in one family
decisions.reason: Readable says what it means that they are all brothers and sisters.

decisions.choice: hermanos, with no gender span; also no span in verse 12
decisions.reason: The English has {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}. Spanish "hermanos" already includes sisters (meaning decision m3), so there is no second wording for the setting. In verse 12 the Spanish reflexive ("se ensalce") names no gender, so the English span on "themselves" has no counterpart either.

decisions.choice: maître for the teacher
decisions.reason: The same word as the address "Maître" (22:16, 22:36) and the explanation of "Rabbi" in 23:7, so the reader sees that the one teacher is the one the others called "Maître". It is lowercase because it is not a title here.

decisions.choice: ndugu, with no gender span; also none in verse 12
alternatives: ndugu wa kiume na wa kike
decisions.reason: The English has {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}. Swahili "ndugu" already means brothers and sisters alike (meaning decision m3), so the setting has nothing to change. In verse 12 the reflexive verb ("atakayejiinua") names no gender either.

decisions.choice: "Thầy", capitalised, for the one teacher
decisions.reason: The meaning decision says the one teacher is Jesus himself; "Thầy" is the noun his disciples use for him, and the capital shows who is meant.

decisions.choice: "{{gender:anh chị em|anh em}}"
decisions.reason: The style guide's span for adelphoi meaning fellow believers, women and men alike (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: {{gender:형제자매|형제}} for adelphoi
decisions.reason: The settled Korean span for adelphoi meaning fellow members of God's family, women and men alike (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "선생은 한 분" (L, B); "선생님은 오직 한 분" (R)
decisions.reason: The one teacher is Jesus himself (meaning decision); "한 분" keeps the respect, though he speaks of himself; Readable uses the word people used to address him.

source.text: καὶ πατέρα μὴ καλέσητε ὑμῶν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, εἷς γάρ ἐστιν ὑμῶν ὁ πατὴρ ὁ οὐράνιος·

records.literal_gloss: And father not call of you on the earth, one for is of you the Father the heavenly;

en.L: And do not call [anyone] on earth your father, for one is your Father, the heavenly [one].
en.B: And do not give anyone on earth the title 'father,' because you have one Father, the one in heaven.
en.R: And do not call any person on earth your 'father' as a title of honor. You have only one Father, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is in heaven.

es.L: Y padre {{plural_you:suyo|vuestro}} no {{plural_you:llamen|llaméis}} [a nadie] sobre la tierra, porque uno es {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Padre, el celestial.
es.B: Y no {{plural_you:den|deis}} a nadie en la tierra el título de “padre”, porque {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} un solo Padre, el que está en el cielo.
es.R: Y no {{plural_you:llamen|llaméis}} “padre” a ninguna persona en la tierra como título de honor. {{plural_you:Tienen|Tenéis}} un solo Padre, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} está en el cielo.

fr.L: Et n’appelez [personne] votre père sur la terre, car un seul est votre Père, le [Père] céleste.
fr.B: Et ne donnez à personne sur la terre le titre de “père”, car vous n’avez qu’un seul Père, celui qui est dans le ciel.
fr.R: Et n’appelez personne sur la terre “père” pour l’honorer. Vous n’avez qu’un seul Père, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est dans le ciel.

sw.L: Na baba yenu msimwite [mtu] juu ya nchi, kwa sababu mmoja ndiye Baba yenu, yule wa mbinguni.
sw.B: Tena msimpe mtu yeyote duniani cheo cha 'baba,' kwa sababu mnaye Baba mmoja, yule aliye mbinguni.
sw.R: Tena msimwite mtu yeyote duniani 'baba' kama cheo cha heshima. Mna Baba mmoja tu, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} yuko mbinguni.

vi.L: Và đừng gọi ai trên đất là cha của các con, vì các con chỉ có một Cha, là Cha trên trời.
vi.B: Cũng đừng gọi ai trên đất là 'cha,' vì các con chỉ có một Cha, là Đấng ở trên trời.
vi.R: Cũng đừng gọi người nào trên đất là 'cha' như một danh hiệu tôn kính. Các con chỉ có một Cha, và Cha ấy ở trên trời.

ko.L: 그리고 땅에서 [아무도] 너희의 아버지라고 부르지 마라. 너희의 아버지는 한 분, 하늘에 계신 분이시기 때문이다.
ko.B: 또 땅에 있는 누구도 '아버지'라고 부르지 마라. 너희의 아버지는 오직 한 분, 하늘에 계신 아버지이시다.
ko.R: 또 세상에 있는 어떤 사람도 너희의 '아버지'라고 높여 부르지 마라. 너희의 아버지는 오직 한 분이시다. 그분은 하늘에 계신다.

pt.L: E não chamem [ninguém] na terra de pai de vocês, pois um só é o Pai de vocês, o celestial.
pt.B: E não deem a ninguém na terra o título de 'pai', porque vocês têm um só Pai, aquele que está no céu.
pt.R: E não chamem nenhuma pessoa na terra de 'pai' como título de honra. Vocês têm um só Pai, e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} está no céu.

am.L: በምድር ላይም [ማንንም] አባታችሁ ብላችሁ አትጥሩ፤ አባታችሁ አንዱ ሰማያዊው ነውና።
am.B: በምድር ላይም ማንንም “አባት” ብላችሁ የማዕረግ ስም አትስጡ፤ አባታችሁ አንድ ነው፤ እርሱም በሰማይ ያለው ነው።
am.R: በምድር ላይ ያለን ማንንም ሰው ለማክበር “አባት” ብላችሁ አትጥሩት። ያላችሁ አባት አንድ ብቻ ነው፤ እርሱም በሰማይ ነው።

decisions.choice: father: a title of honor for revered teachers and ancestors
decisions.reason: Jesus is not forbidding children to call a parent father (15:4-6). Revered teachers and founders were called father, as Israel spoke of "our father Abraham" (3:9).

decisions.choice: the heavenly Father: God, the Father of Jesus's disciples
alternatives: a heavenly being other than God
decisions.reason: Matthew often speaks of "your heavenly Father" (5:48; 6:14, 26, 32).

decisions.choice: as a title of honor
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the word is used here as a title.

decisions.choice: "Cha trên trời" (L) for "the heavenly Father"
alternatives: "Cha ... Đấng ở trên các tầng trời"
decisions.reason: Here the Greek has the adjective "heavenly", not "in the heavens", so Literal does not use the longer phrase, as in 15:13 and 18:35. "Cha" is a noun and takes no deity_pronoun span.

decisions.choice: "Cha ấy ở trên trời" (R) in place of the English "he"
decisions.reason: Readable repeats the noun "Cha", which needs no setting, where the English Readable writes a pronoun with a span; the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: "높여 부르다" (R)
decisions.reason: Father here is a title of honour for revered teachers (meaning decision); Readable says so, as the English does.

source.text: μηδὲ κληθῆτε καθηγηταί, ὅτι καθηγητὴς ὑμῶν ἐστιν εἷς ὁ χριστός·

records.literal_gloss: Nor be called instructors, because instructor of you is one, the Christ;

en.L: Nor be called instructors, because your instructor is one, the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: Do not be called instructors either, because you have one instructor, the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.R: Do not let people call you 'guide' either. You have only one guide, the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.

es.L: Ni {{plural_you:sean llamados|seáis llamados}} instructores, porque {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} instructor es uno, el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}.
es.B: Tampoco {{plural_you:se dejen|os dejéis}} llamar instructores, porque {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} un solo instructor, el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}.
es.R: Tampoco {{plural_you:dejen|dejéis}} que la gente {{plural_you:los|os}} llame “guía”. {{plural_you:Tienen|Tenéis}} un solo guía, el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}.

fr.L: Ne soyez pas non plus appelés guides, parce que votre guide est un seul : le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.B: Ne vous faites pas non plus appeler guides, car vous n’avez qu’un seul guide, le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.R: Ne laissez pas non plus les gens vous appeler “guide”. Vous n’avez qu’un seul guide : le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.

sw.L: Wala msiitwe wakufunzi, kwa sababu mkufunzi wenu ni mmoja, yaani {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.B: Wala msikubali kuitwa wakufunzi, kwa sababu mnaye mkufunzi mmoja, {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.R: Wala msikubali watu wawaite 'kiongozi.' Mna kiongozi mmoja tu, {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.

vi.L: Cũng đừng để người ta gọi mình là người hướng dẫn, vì các con chỉ có một Người Hướng Dẫn, là {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}.
vi.B: Cũng đừng để ai gọi mình là người hướng dẫn, vì các con chỉ có một Người Hướng Dẫn, là {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}.
vi.R: Các con cũng đừng để người ta gọi mình là 'người dẫn đường.' Các con chỉ có một Người Dẫn Đường, là {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}.

ko.L: 또 지도자라고 불리지도 마라. 너희의 지도자는 한 분, {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}이시기 때문이다.
ko.B: 또 너희는 지도자라고 불리지도 마라. 너희의 지도자는 오직 한 분, {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}이시다.
ko.R: 또 사람들이 너희를 '인도자'라고 부르게 하지도 마라. 너희를 인도하는 분은 오직 한 분, {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}이시다.

pt.L: Nem sejam chamados de instrutores, porque o instrutor de vocês é um só, o {{christos:Cristo|Messias}}.
pt.B: Também não sejam chamados de instrutores, porque vocês têm um só instrutor, o {{christos:Cristo|Messias}}.
pt.R: Também não deixem que as pessoas chamem vocês de 'guia'. Vocês têm um só guia, o {{christos:Cristo|Messias}}.

am.L: መሪዎችም ተብላችሁ አትጠሩ፤ መሪያችሁ አንዱ {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሕ}} ነውና።
am.B: ደግሞም መሪዎች ተብላችሁ አትጠሩ፤ መሪያችሁ አንድ ነው፤ እርሱም {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሕ}} ነው።
am.R: ሰዎች “መሪ” ብለው እንዲጠሯችሁም አትፍቀዱ። ያላችሁ መሪ አንድ ብቻ ነው፤ እርሱም {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሕ}} ነው።

decisions.choice: instructor: a teacher who guides others
alternatives: the same word as teacher in 23:8
decisions.reason: This is a different word from the one in 23:8. It was used of a tutor or guide, one who leads others in learning.

decisions.choice: the Christ: Jesus speaks of himself as the Messiah
alternatives: a coming figure other than Jesus
decisions.reason: The title has the article: the Christ, the Messiah. Peter has confessed Jesus to be the Christ (16:16), and here Jesus calls himself his disciples' only instructor.

decisions.choice: guide
decisions.reason: Readable uses a short common word, and keeps it apart from "teacher" in 23:8.

decisions.choice: guides (L, B), as Readable
decisions.reason: The word means a teacher who guides others (m1). French "instructeur" sounds military or like a driving school, "précepteur" like a private tutor, and "maître" is already used for 23:8; "guide" says the sense at every level and keeps the two titles apart.

decisions.choice: wakufunzi (L, B); kiongozi (R)
decisions.reason: The word is a teacher who guides others (meaning decision m1), different from "mwalimu" in verse 8. "Mkufunzi" is an instructor; Readable says "guide", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "người hướng dẫn" (L, B), "người dẫn đường" (R), capitalised for the Christ
decisions.reason: The Greek is a different word from "teacher" in 23:8, one who guides others (meaning decision); "giáo sư" now means a professor. The capital marks the title Jesus gives himself, as "Thầy" in 23:8.

decisions.choice: "{{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}" at every level
decisions.reason: The style guide's span for Christos as a title; "Đấng" carries the sense of the Greek article.

decisions.choice: "지도자" (L, B); "인도자" (R) for kathegetes
decisions.reason: A teacher who guides others (meaning decision), set apart from "선생" in 23:8; Readable's word says the guiding plainly.

decisions.choice: {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}이시다, with the copula outside the span
decisions.reason: Both forms end in a vowel, so one ending fits both.

decisions.choice: "መሪ" (guide) for the instructor
decisions.reason: "አስተማሪ" would be heard as the same word as "መምህር" (teacher) in 23:8, while the Greek uses a different word here, for a teacher who guides. "መሪ" keeps the two titles apart.

source.text: ὁ δὲ μείζων ὑμῶν ἔσται ὑμῶν διάκονος.

records.literal_gloss: The but greater of you will be of you servant.

en.L: But the greatest among you will be your servant.
en.B: Whoever is greatest among you will be the one who serves you.
en.R: The most important person among you must be the one who serves the others.

es.L: Pero el mayor de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} será {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} servidor.
es.B: El más grande entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} será el que {{plural_you:los|os}} sirva.
es.R: La persona más importante entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} debe ser la que sirve a los demás.

fr.L: Mais le plus grand d’entre vous sera votre serviteur.
fr.B: Celui qui est le plus grand parmi vous sera celui qui vous sert.
fr.R: La personne la plus importante parmi vous doit être celle qui sert les autres.

sw.L: Lakini mkubwa zaidi kati yenu atakuwa mhudumu wenu.
sw.B: Yeyote aliye mkubwa kuliko wote kati yenu atakuwa ndiye anayewahudumia.
sw.R: Mtu aliye muhimu kuliko wote kati yenu lazima awe yule anayewahudumia wengine.

vi.L: Nhưng người lớn hơn cả trong các con sẽ là đầy tớ của các con.
vi.B: Ai lớn nhất trong các con sẽ là người phục vụ các con.
vi.R: Người quan trọng nhất trong các con phải là người phục vụ những người khác.

ko.L: 너희 가운데 더 큰 사람은 너희를 섬기는 사람이 될 것이다.
ko.B: 너희 가운데 가장 큰 사람은 너희를 섬기는 사람이 되어야 한다.
ko.R: 너희 가운데 가장 높은 사람은 다른 사람들을 섬기는 사람이어야 한다.

pt.L: Mas o maior de vocês será servo de vocês.
pt.B: Quem for o maior entre vocês será aquele que serve a vocês.
pt.R: A pessoa mais importante entre vocês deve ser aquela que serve os outros.

am.B: ከእናንተ መካከል ታላቅ የሆነ እናንተን የሚያገለግል ይሆናል።
am.R: ከእናንተ መካከል ከሁሉ ይበልጥ አስፈላጊ የሆነው ሰው ሌሎችን የሚያገለግል መሆን አለበት።

decisions.choice: will be: a future with the force of a command
decisions.reason: The future is often used in the law for what must be done. Jesus says how greatness works among his followers.

decisions.choice: servant: one who waits on others
decisions.reason: This is the word for one who serves at table, not the word for slave. Jesus has said the same in 20:26-27.

decisions.choice: the greatest: the comparative used for the highest
alternatives: the one who is greater than one other
decisions.reason: In the Greek of this time the comparative "greater" often means "greatest" (18:1, 4).

decisions.choice: must be
decisions.reason: Readable gives the force of the future as a command, from the first meaning decision.

decisions.choice: mhudumu
decisions.reason: The word is one who waits on others (meaning decision m2), the word used for the attendants in 22:13, not the slave ("mtumwa", "mtumishi"). "Mhudumu" keeps that sense.

decisions.choice: "lớn hơn cả" (L), "lớn nhất" (B), "quan trọng nhất" (R); "đầy tớ" (L), "người phục vụ" (B, R) for diakonos
decisions.reason: As in 18:1 for the comparative used as a superlative. The Greek is diakonos, one who waits on others, not doulos, so even Literal does not say "nô lệ".

decisions.choice: "더 큰" (L), "가장 큰" (B), "가장 높은" (R); "될 것이다" (L), "되어야 한다" (B, R); "섬기는 사람"
decisions.reason: The comparative is used for the highest, and the future has the force of a command (meaning decision); Literal keeps both forms. Diakonos is "섬기는 사람", not "종", which stays for doulos.

decisions.choice: servo
decisions.reason: The word is the one for a person who waits on others, not for a slave (m2), so "escravo" is wrong; "servidor" now suggests a civil servant, and "diácono" a church office. Balanced and Readable say what the servant does, as the English does.

source.text: ὅστις δὲ ὑψώσει ἑαυτὸν ταπεινωθήσεται, καὶ ὅστις ταπεινώσει ἑαυτὸν ὑψωθήσεται.

records.literal_gloss: Whoever but will exalt himself will be humbled, and whoever will humble himself will be exalted.

en.L: And whoever exalts {{gender:themselves|himself}} will be humbled, and whoever humbles {{gender:themselves|himself}} will be exalted.
en.B: Those who lift themselves up will be brought low, and those who make themselves low will be lifted up.
en.R: If people try to make themselves important, God will bring them down. But if people make themselves humble, God will lift them up.

es.L: Y el que se ensalce a sí mismo será humillado, y el que se humille a sí mismo será ensalzado.
es.B: Los que se ponen por encima serán rebajados, y los que se rebajan serán puestos en alto.
es.R: Si alguien trata de hacerse importante, Dios lo hará bajar. Pero si alguien se hace humilde, Dios lo levantará.

fr.L: Et celui qui s’élèvera lui-même sera abaissé, et celui qui s’abaissera lui-même sera élevé.
fr.B: Ceux qui se haussent seront rabaissés, et ceux qui se font petits seront élevés.
fr.R: Si des gens essaient de se rendre importants, Dieu les fera descendre. Mais si des gens se font humbles, Dieu les élèvera.

sw.L: Na yeyote atakayejiinua atanyenyekezwa, na yeyote atakayejinyenyekeza atainuliwa.
sw.B: Wanaojiinua watashushwa chini, na wanaojishusha watainuliwa juu.
sw.R: Watu wakijaribu kujifanya kuwa wakubwa, Mungu atawashusha. Lakini watu wakijinyenyekeza, Mungu atawainua.

vi.L: Ai tự tôn mình lên sẽ bị hạ xuống, và ai tự hạ mình xuống sẽ được tôn lên.
vi.B: Ai tự nâng mình lên sẽ bị hạ xuống, còn ai tự hạ mình xuống sẽ được nâng lên.
vi.R: Ai tìm cách làm cho mình trở nên quan trọng, Đức Chúa Trời sẽ hạ người ấy xuống. Nhưng ai tự hạ mình, Đức Chúa Trời sẽ nâng người ấy lên.

ko.L: 누구든지 자기를 높이는 사람은 낮아질 것이고, 누구든지 자기를 낮추는 사람은 높아질 것이다.
ko.B: 자기를 높이는 사람은 낮아지고, 자기를 낮추는 사람은 높아질 것이다.
ko.R: 누구든지 스스로 높아지려고 하면, 하나님께서 그 사람을 낮추실 것이다. 그러나 누구든지 스스로 낮추면, 하나님께서 그 사람을 높여 주실 것이다.

pt.L: E quem se exaltar será humilhado, e quem se humilhar será exaltado.
pt.B: Os que se colocam no alto serão rebaixados, e os que se fazem pequenos serão elevados.
pt.R: Se as pessoas tentam se fazer importantes, Deus vai rebaixá-las. Mas, se as pessoas se fazem humildes, Deus vai elevá-las.

am.L: ራሱን ከፍ የሚያደርግ ሁሉ ዝቅ ይደረጋል፤ ራሱንም ዝቅ የሚያደርግ ሁሉ ከፍ ይደረጋል።
am.B: ራሳቸውን ከፍ የሚያደርጉ ዝቅ ይደረጋሉ፤ ራሳቸውን ዝቅ የሚያደርጉም ከፍ ይደረጋሉ።
am.R: ሰዎች ራሳቸውን ትልቅ ለማድረግ ቢሞክሩ እግዚአብሔር ዝቅ ያደርጋቸዋል። ራሳቸውን ዝቅ ቢያደርጉ ግን እግዚአብሔር ከፍ ያደርጋቸዋል።

decisions.choice: will be humbled, will be exalted: God is the one who acts
alternatives: people will humble or honor them
decisions.reason: The passive voice often points to God without naming him. The final reversal is his doing.

decisions.choice: exalting and humbling: a theme of the Scriptures
decisions.reason: God brings down the proud and lifts up the lowly (1 Samuel 2:7-8; Proverbs 29:23; Ezekiel 21:26). Jesus has said the same of the child-like in 18:4.

decisions.choice: {{gender:themselves|himself}}
decisions.reason: The saying is about anyone, so the inclusive form is the default.

decisions.choice: those who; if people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the plural, which covers everyone without a pronoun choice.

decisions.choice: God will bring them down; God will lift them up
alternatives: will be humbled; will be exalted
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who acts, from the first meaning decision.

decisions.choice: celui qui ... lui-même, with no gender span (L)
decisions.reason: English Literal needs {{gender:themselves|himself}}; French "celui qui" and the "lui-même" that refers back to it are ordinary generic French, so, as the style guide says, they take no span. Balanced and Readable use the plural, as in English.

decisions.choice: "ai ... mình" with no gender span
decisions.reason: The reflexive "mình" and "ai" already take in men and women, so the English themselves/himself setting has no Vietnamese counterpart.

decisions.choice: No gender span: "누구든지", "자기", "그 사람"
alternatives: a span as in the English Literal
decisions.reason: Korean reflexive "자기" and "누구든지" are already inclusive; the wording of the Korean Luke 14:11.

decisions.choice: "하나님께서" (R)
decisions.reason: God is the one who acts (meaning decision); Readable names him, as the English does.

decisions.choice: quem se exaltar ... quem se humilhar, with no gender setting
alternatives: quem se exaltar a si mesmo, with a gender setting
decisions.reason: The English needs a setting to choose between "themselves" and "himself". Portuguese "quem" and the reflexive "se" carry no gender, so the saying is already about anyone.

decisions.choice: "ራሱን ... ሁሉ" (whoever ... himself) with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span like the English {{gender:themselves|himself}}
decisions.reason: Amharic uses the masculine "ራሱን ... ሁሉ" for anyone at all, women and men, so it has no second wording here; Balanced and Readable use the plural, as the English does.
